title: Steve Jobs's late notes: Pixar-style products for everybody, gratitude, and organ donation (2007-2010)
summary: A collection of Steve's late emails and speeches. He explains why Apple designs products for everybody the way Pixar makes films, says a company is only as good as its next product, and reflects on how dependent every person is on the work of others. He also pushes organ donation with "one simple question."

principles.text: Design for everybody, not a narrow target demographic, the way Pixar makes films for every layer of the family.
principles.quote: we don’t think, “Oh, well, our target audience is fifteen to twenty-nine, male.” We don’t think that way. We think about making a great product for just about everybody.

principles.text: Software lets one great device be tailored to do almost anything.
principles.quote: the beauty of the products we make is they can be tailored with software to do almost anything.

principles.text: Past wins, even passing Microsoft, don't matter. You are only as good as your next amazing product.
principles.quote: Walt Disney used to say to his team: “We’re only as good as our next picture.” Well, we’re only as good as our next amazing new product.

principles.text: Take a moment to reflect on success, but know that glory is fleeting and go back to work.
principles.quote: Stocks go up and down, and things may be different tomorrow, but I thought it was worth a moment of reflection today.

principles.text: Meaningful work is work you can proudly explain to your kids.
principles.quote: We can say, “I worked on our next-generation iPad. You know, the ones that you use in school.” And that’s a really wonderful thing.

principles.text: Every person depends on the creations of countless others, so love and admire humanity and be grateful.
principles.quote: I love and admire my species, living and dead, and am totally dependent on them for my life and well being.
